newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech president has doubts about govt programme.
newsitem.headline: Czech president has doubts about govt programme.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel said on Thursday that he was pleased that leaders of the ruling centre-right coalition were ready to deal with the country's economic turmoil, but he had doubts over the way the coalition agreed to do it.
In a statement, he said that while the economic stabilisation programme agreed on Wednesday may address short term difficulties, it did not deal with longer term questions.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and leaders of the two junior coalition parties agreed on Wednesday to an austerity programme of unspecified budget cuts and public sector wage freezes and ministerial changes aimed at halting a crisis of confidence in the Czech crown and the economy.
Education Minister Ivan Pilip is to take over as Finance Minister and the current Czech ambassador to Britain Karel Kuhnl will be the new Trade and Industry Minister.

In listing what he called "several doubts", Havel said the plan "still does not mention even a word about long-term programme aims of this coalition and government, and does not, in the new situation, develop and make concrete its programme statement."
Havel said it did not offer "even a word" of who was responsible for the economic crisis, and that he could not understand the connection between the cabinet changes -- and the new programme.
Still, he said he indicated he might confirm the cabinet changes on Monday.
